semantic_correction.stem: An average-risk client age 30 to 65 chooses cervical cancer screening with high-risk HPV testing plus cervical cytology (co-testing) after counseling. According to current ACOG guidance, which screening interval is acceptable?
semantic_correction.rationale: ACOG Committee Statement No. 28, published in 2026, states that for average-risk individuals age 30 to 65 years, clinician-collected primary high-risk HPV screening every 5 years is preferred. Co-testing with high-risk HPV testing plus cervical cytology every 5 years remains an acceptable alternative when primary hrHPV testing is not available or when, after counseling, the patient chooses co-testing. Therefore a 5-year interval is acceptable for the co-testing strategy described in the stem.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply current cervical cancer screening guidance by recognizing a 5-year interval for hrHPV/cytology co-testing in average-risk clients age 30 to 65 when co-testing is selected.
semantic_correction.source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)

semantic_correction.source_locator: Summary of Recommendations — individuals age 30–65: clinician-collected primary hrHPV screening every 5 years preferred; co-testing with hrHPV and cervical cytology every 5 years acceptable when primary hrHPV testing is not available or the patient chooses co-testing after counseling
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: ACOG's 2026 guidance accepts hrHPV/cytology co-testing every 5 years for average-risk individuals age 30–65 when co-testing is selected after counseling or primary hrHPV testing is unavailable.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only once' absolute distractor, kept the current 2026 ACOG co-testing interval, and balanced all answer choices as plausible interval options.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Committee Statement No. 28, Summary of Recommendations
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preventive screening
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests the current 5-year co-testing interval for average-risk adults age 30–65 when co-testing is selected.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. Annual co-testing is more frequent than the current recommended interval for average-risk adults.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Three years applies to certain other cervical-screening strategies, not clinician-collected hrHPV/cytology co-testing in this scenario.
option_audit.C: Correct. ACOG accepts co-testing every 5 years for average-risk individuals age 30–65 under the stated conditions.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. A 10-year interval is longer than the recommended co-testing interval.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. C alone matches the specific co-testing interval in current ACOG guidance.
cueing_check: All four alternatives are concise screening intervals with no absolute-word or answer-length cue.
